What happens to my Telegram when I die?

By the Afterkeep research team · Reviewed on 2 Nov 2026

Short answer: Telegram has no deceased-user process or legacy contact. Instead, accounts self-destruct: if an account doesn't come online for the period set in Settings (18 months by default), Telegram deletes it along with all its messages, media and contacts in the Telegram cloud. Secret chats exist only on the original device. To keep anything, export it with Telegram Desktop before it's gone.

Key facts

  • No deceased-user process or legacy contact
  • Inactive accounts self-destruct (18 months by default)
  • Secret chats exist only on the original device
  • Export with Telegram Desktop's Export Telegram data tool

How do I prepare my Telegram account?

  1. Check your self-destruct period in Settings, Privacy and Security, and pick one that gives family time to export what they need.
  2. Keep the phone number, any 2-Step Verification password and the phone's passcode in a password manager with emergency access. Telegram logs in with a code sent to the number or to a logged-in device.
  3. Export chats you want kept: Telegram Desktop has an Export Telegram data tool that saves chats and media offline as HTML or JSON.
  4. Remember that secret chats are device-specific and aren't in the cloud, so they can't be exported from another device.
  5. After a death: if a device is still logged in, family can export chats with Telegram Desktop or delete the account at telegram.org/deactivate (the code arrives in Telegram, not by SMS).
  6. Otherwise, do nothing: the account deletes itself after the self-destruct period. Contacts keep their own copies of messages the person sent them.

Read the official policy ↗

What documents do heirs need?

  • Access to a logged-in device, or the phone number and any 2-Step Verification password
  • Telegram publishes no document-based process for families

How long does it take?

If the account doesn't come online for the self-destruct period (18 months by default, adjustable in Settings), Telegram deletes it with all its cloud data. Deleting an account manually is immediate and irreversible.

What can't be recovered?

  • All messages, media and contacts in the Telegram cloud when the account self-destructs or is deleted
  • Secret chats, which never leave the original device
  • Groups the person created stay, but without a creator (admins keep their rights)

Frequently asked questions

What happens to my Telegram when I die?

Telegram has no deceased-user process or legacy contact. Instead, accounts self-destruct: if an account doesn't come online for the period set in Settings (18 months by default), Telegram deletes it along with all its messages, media and contacts in the Telegram cloud. Secret chats exist only on the original device. To keep anything, export it with Telegram Desktop before it's gone.

What happens to my Telegram account when I die?

If nobody logs in, it self-destructs after the period set in Settings (18 months by default) and Telegram deletes all its messages, media and contacts. Telegram publishes no process for families.

Can family get into a dead person's Telegram?

Telegram offers no family access process. Logging in needs a code sent to the phone number or a logged-in device, so plan ahead with a password manager.

How do I save Telegram chats before they're deleted?

Use Telegram Desktop's Export Telegram data tool, which saves chats and media offline as HTML or JSON. Secret chats are device-specific and can't be exported from another device.

How do I delete a deceased person's Telegram account?

With access to a logged-in device, delete it at telegram.org/deactivate (the code arrives in Telegram). Otherwise it self-deletes after the self-destruct period.

Do contacts lose messages when an account is deleted?

No. Telegram says contacts keep their copy of messages the person sent them, and groups the person created keep running.
